requirements.title: Federal Employer Identification Number (EIN) for the partnership
requirements.quote: Generally, you need an EIN to: Hire employees Operate a partnership or corporation Pay sales and excise taxes Change business structures or ownership Administer certain trusts, retirement plans and estates
requirements.notes: A general partnership needs its own EIN; get it first because the partnership's tax returns and state registrations ask for it.

requirements.title: Register the trade name or report the fictitious name (Second Stitch Vintage)
requirements.quote: The fictitious name report shall be accompanied by a filing fee of thirty-nine dollars ... A report under this division shall be made within thirty days after the date of the first use of the fictitious name.
requirements.notes: Either a trade name registration (exclusive use) or a fictitious name report satisfies R.C. 1329.01; a general partnership lists at least one partner, and filings last five years.

requirements.title: Ohio vendor's license for the home (fixed) place of business
requirements.agency: Ohio Department of Taxation (issued for the Franklin County Auditor)
requirements.quote: Vendor $50 A person or business selling taxable goods from a fixed location in Ohio. Each location needs a separate license. This includes physical storefront locations and selling items online within Ohio.
requirements.notes: Clothing is taxable in Ohio; the page also says any person making taxable sales must first obtain a vendor license, and the fee rose from $25 to $50 on April 9, 2025.

requirements.title: Ohio transient vendor's license for pop-up markets
requirements.condition: Selling at pop-up markets or shows in Ohio counties other than Franklin County
requirements.quote: Transient Vendor $50 A person or business selling taxable goods from temporary locations (shows, flea markets, etc.) ... The license is valid statewide.
requirements.notes: R.C. 5739.17 lets a regular vendor's license holder sell at temporary events in its own county without a transient license, so it is needed only for events outside Franklin County.

requirements.title: File Ohio sales tax returns
requirements.quote: All businesses who are registered for an Ohio Vendor License are required to file a sales return until the license is closed with the Department of Taxation.
requirements.notes: Returns are due by the 23rd after each period (monthly, or semi-annual if liability is under $1,200 per six months), including periods with no sales.

requirements.title: Collect and remit Ohio sales tax on Etsy orders
requirements.quote: This means the company is treated as the actual seller for all sales it helps make. Because of that, it must register for a seller’s use tax license, collect sales tax from buyers in Ohio
requirements.notes: Etsy, as a marketplace facilitator with Ohio nexus, collects and remits Ohio tax on sales it facilitates; the partners still collect on their own website and pop-up sales.

requirements.title: Keep secondhand purchase records and post a sign (R.C. 4737.01)
requirements.agency: State of Ohio (enforced by local law enforcement)
requirements.quote: A person ... purchasing, selling, exchanging, or receiving secondhand articles of any kind ... shall keep a separate record book or electronic file in which shall be written ... the name, description, and residence of the person from whom purchased
requirements.notes: No license, but buyers of secondhand goods must record each purchase with a copy of the seller's ID, keep records one year, post a sign, and not buy from minors or between 9 p.m. and 7 a.m. (R.C. 4737.03).

requirements.title: Do not resell recalled products; check children's clothing rules
requirements.quote: Resellers are required by law to know the recall status of the products they sell. It is illegal to sell any recalled product.
requirements.notes: If they sell children's clothing, the guide's drawstring and flammability rules for children's items also apply.

requirements.title: File the Columbus business (net profit) income tax return, Form BR-25
requirements.agency: City of Columbus Income Tax Division
requirements.quote: Columbus requires that the partnership (or LLC) pay all tax due on behalf of all affected partners.
requirements.notes: The partnership files BR-25 by the 15th day of the fourth month after year end (April 15 for calendar year), even if it reports a net loss; the city rate is 2.5%.

requirements.title: Columbus quarterly estimated income tax payments
requirements.agency: City of Columbus Income Tax Division
requirements.condition: Partnership expects to owe $200 or more in Columbus income tax for the year
requirements.quote: Individuals and Businesses expecting to owe $200.00 or more in Columbus income tax for the current year are required to make quarterly estimated tax payments.
requirements.notes: At 2.5%, this is reached once Columbus net profit is about $8,000.

requirements.title: Columbus home occupation rules for running the business from home
requirements.agency: City of Columbus Building and Zoning Services
requirements.quote: J. No wholesale or retail business, including the sale or transfer of any firearm shall be conducted in a dwelling unit.
requirements.notes: No home occupation permit appears in the city's provisions sheet, BZS FAQ or forms list; whether online retail with inventory stored at home is allowed under rule J, and whether a non-resident sibling may work there (rule E), is not settled by official pages.

requirements.title: Columbus itinerant vendor or commercial sales license for pop-ups in the city
requirements.agency: City of Columbus Building and Zoning Services, License Section
requirements.fee: $20 application + $120/day itinerant vendor license + $32 background check
requirements.quote: Fees: Application $20.00 Itinerant Vendor license $120.00/day BCI Background Check $32.00
requirements.notes: Columbus licenses itinerant vendors (C.C. 517) and commercial sales (C.C. 523, $150 annual), but no city page says whether a vendor at an organized pop-up market needs one; searched columbus.gov License Section pages and application packets.

requirements.title: Columbus secondhand dealer license
requirements.agency: City of Columbus Building and Zoning Services, License Section
requirements.quote: Below is a complete list of licenses that the License Section issues.
requirements.notes: The list has scrap metal dealers but no secondhand, junk or pawn dealer license, and no general business license.

requirements.title: File a partnership registration or statement with the Secretary of State
requirements.quote: A partnership may file a statement of partnership authority.
requirements.notes: Optional for a general partnership; the name filing under R.C. 1329.01 is the required step.

requirements.title: Ohio Commercial Activity Tax (CAT)
requirements.quote: For tax years 2025 and forward: Businesses with more than $6 million a year in Ohio TGR need to pay the CAT.
requirements.notes: Registration is required only within 30 days of exceeding $6 million in Ohio taxable gross receipts.

requirements.title: Ohio tangible personal property (inventory) tax return
requirements.quote: The state’s final tangible personal property tax returns are due from businesses on Wednesday, April 30. The returns will cover the 2008 tax year, the last for the tangible personal property tax in Ohio.
requirements.notes: Ohio no longer taxes business inventory or equipment, so stored vintage stock needs no property tax filing.

requirements.title: Ohio pass-through entity withholding return (IT 1140)
requirements.condition: Only if a partner is not an Ohio resident (a qualifying investor) and the adjusted qualifying amount exceeds $1,000
requirements.quote: A qualifying pass-through entity (PTE) is required to file an Ohio IT 1140 when the PTE: Is doing business in Ohio or otherwise has nexus with Ohio Has at least one qualifying investor
requirements.notes: If both siblings are full-year Ohio residents, no IT 1140 or IT 4708 is needed; each reports their share on their own Ohio return.

requirements.title: Ohio estimated personal income tax payments
requirements.condition: A partner's Ohio tax minus credits and withholding is more than $500
requirements.quote: You should make estimated payments if your estimated Ohio tax liability (total tax minus total credits) less Ohio withholding is more than $500.
requirements.notes: Applies to each partner individually on their share of partnership income.

requirements.title: Federal partnership return (Form 1065) and Schedules K-1
requirements.quote: A partnership must file an annual information return to report the income, deductions, gains, losses, etc., from its operations, but it does not pay income tax.
requirements.notes: The partnership must also furnish each partner a Schedule K-1.

requirements.title: Self-employment tax for each partner
requirements.quote: You must pay self-employment tax and file Schedule SE (Form 1040) if either of the following applies. Your net earnings from self-employment (excluding church employee income) were $400 or more.
requirements.notes: Each partner's share of partnership earnings counts toward their own $400 test and Schedule SE.

requirements.title: Federal quarterly estimated tax payments for each partner
requirements.condition: A partner expects to owe $1,000 or more when filing
requirements.quote: Individuals, including sole proprietors, partners, and S corporation shareholders, generally have to make estimated tax payments if they expect to owe tax of $1,000 or more when their return is filed.
requirements.notes: Applies to partners individually, not to the partnership.

requirements.title: Federal business license or permit
requirements.quote: Business activities regulated by a federal agency will need a federal license or permit.
requirements.notes: Reselling used clothing is not a federally licensed activity.

requirements.title: Beneficial ownership information (BOI) report
requirements.quote: U.S. companies are exempt from the Beneficial Ownership Information (BOI) reporting requirements and therefore, are no longer required to file BOI reports.
requirements.notes: A general partnership formed without a state filing was never a reporting company, and the final rule exempts U.S. companies.

hard_calls.about: Columbus home occupation rules versus a home-based online resale business
hard_calls.explanation: The city's home occupation provisions list no permit, but rule J says no wholesale or retail business shall be conducted in a dwelling unit, rule F requires storage inside the residence, and rule E bars non-residents from working there. Official pages don't say whether online/Etsy sales shipped from home count as a retail business in the dwelling, or whether the sibling who doesn't live there may work there.

hard_calls.about: Local vendor licenses for pop-up markets (Columbus and other Ohio cities)
hard_calls.explanation: Columbus issues Itinerant Vendor (C.C. 517, $120/day plus $1,000 bond) and Commercial Sales (C.C. 523) licenses, and both packets require a state transient vendor's license for taxable goods even though state law lets a Franklin County vendor's license cover events in that county. The code chapters defining who needs them are not on a city-run site, and other host cities may have their own peddler rules.

hard_calls.about: Scope of Ohio's secondhand-article recordkeeping law
hard_calls.explanation: R.C. 4737.01(B) literally covers any person purchasing or selling secondhand articles of any kind, which includes vintage clothing, but no Ohio agency page explains whether it reaches purchases from thrift stores, estate sales or online sellers versus walk-in sellers. Columbus issues no secondhand dealer license.

hard_calls.about: Reporting Etsy sales on the partnership's own Ohio sales tax return
hard_calls.explanation: Ohio says the marketplace facilitator is treated as the seller for facilitated sales, but the pages checked don't say whether an in-state vendor with its own license must list Etsy-facilitated sales on its return. Ohio also keeps origin sourcing for an Ohio vendor's own in-state sales while marketplaces source to the buyer's location.

hard_calls.about: Ohio Secretary of State pages blocked; name filing timing
hard_calls.explanation: ohiosos.gov returned 403 to automated fetches, so the name rule is cited from the Revised Code. R.C. 1329.01 allows a fictitious name report within 30 days after first use, so it need not precede the first sale, but R.C. 1329.10 bars suing in the name until filed.
New vendor's and transient vendor's licenses cost $50 since April 9, 2025 (R.C. 5739.17 as amended); many older state and county pages still show $25.
